summary: Iteration 4: Full backend + frontend testing of new HRMS & Payroll module (Phase 1). Wrote 29 pytest cases covering lookups, settings, seed, employees CRUD+filters+documents, attendance (upsert/derived compute/bulk/monthly register), leaves (apply/approve auto-attendance/balance/validation), payroll (generate/list/summary/PF/ESIC math), dashboard (all cards, trends), 5 report exports, and regression on legacy /api/resources & /api/expenses endpoints. All 29 tests PASSED. Frontend verified: sidebar nav-hrms present, dashboard KPI cards all render with real data (8 employees, ₹12,410 monthly payroll, ₹2,487 PF, ₹614 ESIC), Employees page renders 8 rows and name validation toast fires, Attendance renders 8 rows with Save button, Leaves/Payroll/Reports/Settings pages all render correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: Payroll math correctness verified: PF employee = 12% of min(basic+da, 15000); ESIC skipped when gross > 21000; net = gross - total_deductions. All match spec.
Attendance derived compute correctly returns working_hours=9.5, overtime=0.5, late_minutes=30 for 09:30-19:00 shift (9h + 15min late threshold).
Leave approval correctly cascades to attendance rows (verified 3 Leave-status rows created for a 3-day leave).
Employee delete correctly cascades to attendance/leaves/payroll collections.
Minor: /api/hrms/leaves apply_leave doesn't validate from_date <= to_date (silently swaps via _days_between); acceptable but could return 400 if reversed.
Minor: React hydration warning on Leaves page about <span> inside <option> — caused by external Emergent dev-tool metadata injection (x-excluded='true'), NOT a code bug. Ignore.
hrms.py file is 1152 lines — consider splitting into hrms/employees.py, hrms/attendance.py, hrms/payroll.py etc. for maintainability (>700 line guideline).
seed_data_creation: Reused already-seeded 8 employees + today's attendance + current-month payroll. Test-created TEST_ employees cleaned up during CRUD test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: HRMS Phase 1 is fully green. Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_hrms.py can be reused for regression. All data-testids in place. Regression on resources+expenses endpoints continues to pass.
